text:
Priya: Quick thread — we need a tight benchmark narrative for launch. Goal: show clear tokens->$ story + a latency distro that explains tail risk. Two visuals max. Thoughts?
Marco: Love the constraint. One hero stat (e.g., 3x lower token cost) + one context viz (latency CDF) -> keeps copy simple.
Ethan: Agree. For hero metric we should tie to concrete workload: 'chat with 1k prompt tokens' style so buyers can map.
Lena: Suggest headline variants to test: 1) 'Lower token cost, same quality' 2) 'Predictable latency, cheaper at scale' — run A/B in page CTA.
Ben: For the latency viz, prefer a CDF instead of pX bars so customers see tail. Example axes:```
X: latency (ms)
Y: cumulative % requests (0-100)
Lines: Redwood vs Competitor A vs Competitor B
```
Marco: Nice. For tokens->$ waterfall, show nominal p50 token cost, then caching/batching savings, then quantization delta. Make the waterfall additive so it reads left-to-right.
Priya: Webinar idea: 20-min demo + 15-min Q&A. Demo shows real-time perf on a 3-worker burst, then a slide comparing per-token $ across traffic slices. We can gate recording for MQL capture.
Ethan: Inbound routing: add a hidden UTM for benchmark traffic -> route heavy usage orgs to sales-led flow, SMBs to self-serve nurture. 
Lena: Messaging nuance — enterprise cares about SLA + isolation. Add a microcopy line under hero: 'Available hosted, dedicated, and private deployment.' keeps it inclusive.
Ben: Copy note: avoid vague 'faster' claims. Use concrete %/x numbers and call out what was held equal (model, sequence length, batch settings).
Priya: Ops question: can we get p95/p99 telemetry slices by model family to display in appendix? OpsBot: Telemetry export scheduled; will push a prefiltered CSV by EOD.
Marco: For landing page CTAs: 1) 'Run the benchmark' (self-serve script) 2) 'Request an enterprise demo' (for high-usage UTM). A/B test primary button copy.
Priya: I'll draft the two hero headlines + chart drafts and share a lightweight Figma today. If OpsBot pushes CSV, we can generate viz prototypes by tomorrow. Everyone OK with that plan? :thumbsup:
